name: RZA
hook: The Wu-Tang Clan's producer and strategist, who made the group's sound and the deal that spread it.
blurb: Robert Diggs was born in Brooklyn and grew up partly on Staten Island. His first solo record, as Prince Rakeem, came out on Tommy Boy in 1991 and did not sell, which is part of the story he tells about why the Wu-Tang Clan was set up the way it was. He then planned the group with his cousins GZA and Ol' Dirty Bastard, and produced nearly all their early music. He was both its producer and the author of its business plan, and both came from one idea: one central sound, spread through many outlets. He traded his SP-1200 for an Ensoniq EPS-16 Plus and used it to make long, sad loops like the one on 'C.R.E.A.M.'. His style of dusty soul loops, out-of-tune piano and film dialogue defined the group's first wave of solo albums. He later wrote music for films, including Jim Jarmusch's Ghost Dog.
